Context: In this excerpt from a letter written by Jefferson after he left government, he discusses the recent signing of the Treaty of Ghent, which ended the War of `text(1812)`.
Title: Source 3: [Adapted from] a Letter to Lafayette (1815)
Author: by Thomas Jefferson
Content: Today I received news of our peace. I am glad of it. And especially glad that we ended the war with the action at New Orleans. But I consider the peace as a cease-fire only, because no security is provided against the impressment of our sailors. With this unsettled, we are in hostility of mind with England, although actual deeds of warfare may be suspended by a truce. The `text(first)` act of impressment she commits on an American will be answered by retaliation, or by declaration of war here. The meantime must be a state of preparation for it. In this time, we have much to do in further strengthening our seaport towns, providing military supplies, preparing and training our militia, and arranging our financial system. And above all pushing our domestic manufactures, which have become so important that they never again can be shaken.
